findings.evidence: cassert-sql-safety.yml push: `paths-ignore:` at line 21 and `paths: ['theodb_rs/src/**', ...]` at line 25 coexist under the same `push:`; pull_request repeats it at lines 31/35. Verified sibling coexistence via grep: license-gate.yml 19/23, lint-rust.yml 18/22 & 28/32, schema-drift-gate.yml 29/33.
findings.message: The `push` (and `pull_request`) event declares BOTH `paths-ignore:` (line 21 / line 31) AND `paths:` (line 25 / line 35). GitHub Actions does not support both path filters for the same event — when both are present it honours `paths` and ignores `paths-ignore`. Since the existing `paths:` globs (`theodb_rs/src/**`, `Cargo.*`, `scripts/cassert-smoke.sh`, the workflow file) already exclude `.claude/**`, `**/*.md` and `docs/**`, the added `paths-ignore` block is inert: it neither adds nor changes filtering, yet reads as load-bearing. Same redundant/misleading combination in license-gate.yml (19+23), lint-rust.yml (18+22, 28+32) and schema-drift-gate.yml (29+33). (ci.yml and ci-canary.yml correctly use ONLY paths-ignore.)
findings.remediation: Drop the redundant `paths-ignore` from the four workflows that already have a code-scoped `paths:` filter (it is a no-op there); keep `paths-ignore` only where there is no `paths:` (ci.yml, ci-canary.yml).

findings.evidence: license-gate.yml job d1 runs 'cargo deny check licenses' on Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock/deny.toml changes; header: 'A allowlist do theodb_rs/deny.toml é fail-closed: licença desconhecida FALHA'. Root NOTICE declares own-code + 'No copyleft (GPL/AGPL) source is used' and reproduces PostgreSQL-License notices for pgvector/pgvectorscale/PostgreSQL/plpython3u with pinned refs.

Combined with a comprehensive root NOTICE that reproduces the PostgreSQL-License notices for every redistributed third-party component, the project's provenance posture is strong.

findings.evidence: linha 57: `BASE="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}"` (identico na linha 84). Nao ha campo free-text (title/body/head_ref) sendo interpolado no shell — so `.sha`/`.before`.
findings.message: `${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}` e interpolado diretamente num bloco `run:` de shell (tambem na linha 84). A guia de hardening do GitHub Actions (CWE-94 script injection) recomenda passar `github.event.*` via `env:` e nunca inline no shell. Aqui o valor e um SHA de commit (hex, validado pelo GitHub), entao NAO e exploravel — defesa-em-profundidade, nao um defeito ativo.
findings.remediation: Vincular a um `env:` do step (`BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}`) e referenciar `"$BASE_SHA"` no script, seguindo o padrao de hardening do GitHub Actions.

findings.evidence: profile_columnar_scan.sh:90-94: "[ \"$nsamples\" -ge 500 ] || fail ... flamegraph seria vacuo (EC-1)"; :117-122 CPU/IO axis derived from folded frames (pread|FileRead|mdread|io_uring > 5% => I/O-BOUND). CHANGELOG 0.140.0: "~80% do tempo e a materializacao de cada linha como heap-tuple ... a descompressao das colunas e so ~7%".
findings.message: Profiling harness data-flow — addressed: the M148 flamegraph harness enforces a >=500-sample floor (EC-1) so an empty capture cannot prioritise the wrong milestone, profiles two representative queries (EC-2) over the REAL 105-column ClickBench schema, and derives the CPU-vs-I/O axis from the captured folded stacks rather than a fragile attached perf-stat. The measured verdict (scan is ~100% CPU-bound, ~80% per-row heap-tuple materialisation, ~7% column decode) corrected the initial code hypothesis by evidence — the correct observability discipline for a hot path.

findings.evidence: Line 92: `nsamples=$(perf script -i "$DATA/$label.perf" 2>/dev/null | grep -c "^[a-z]" || echo 0)` feeds line 94: `[ "$nsamples" -ge 500 ] || fail "$label: perf capturou $nsamples amostras (< 500) ..."`. `grep -c` on zero matches emits '0' + exit 1, so the `|| echo 0` appends a second '0'.
findings.message: `nsamples=$(perf script ... | grep -c "^[a-z]" || echo 0)` mishandles the zero-match case: `grep -c` prints '0' to stdout AND exits 1 when there are no matches, so `|| echo 0` ALSO runs, making `nsamples` the two-line value `0\n0`. The EC-1 floor gate on line 94 `[ "$nsamples" -ge 500 ]` then hits bash 'integer expression expected' (a malformed integer), not the intended numeric comparison. The gate still fails-closed (the `[` error path triggers `|| fail`), so no false-pass — but the sample-floor is enforced by an accident rather than by the comparison it documents (error-handling / robust exit-status handling).
findings.remediation: Drop the `|| echo 0` and default explicitly: `nsamples=$(perf script ... | grep -c "^[a-z]"); nsamples=${nsamples:-0}` — or count with `awk 'END{print NR}'` which returns one clean integer.

findings.evidence: L93-94 fail-fast `if strategy not in ('head','systematic'): raise ValueError`; L97 `if strategy == 'head'` dispatch selecting the `inner` shell fragment + timeout; L254 argparse `choices=['systematic','head']` constrains the input. Two guarded algorithms, no class ceremony.
findings.message: Strategy (implicit) — applied_correctly: `_ensure_sample(strategy=...)` swaps two interchangeable sampling algorithms (`head` = biased temporal slice vs `systematic` = 1-in-k full scan) at runtime via a minimal if/else. A full class-based Strategy would be over_engineered for two one-line shell-fragment variants (catalog Strategy row: 'Do NOT apply when single algorithm forever' + KISS/YAGNI counterweight).

findings.evidence: run_m128_clickbench.py:82-95: systematic strategy `awk 'NR % {k} == 0' | head -n {n}` with k = HITS_TOTAL_ROWS // n; base dict now carries "sample_strategy": args.sample (:143). Unit test benchmarks/tests/test_clickbench_sample.py asserts the composed shell command per strategy via a mocked subprocess.
findings.message: Benchmark data-flow / measurement honesty — addressed: the sampling path was changed from `head -n` (first-N rows = a narrow temporal slice of the EventTime-ordered dataset, artificially low GROUP BY cardinalities that FAVOUR the vectorized pushdown) to systematic 1-in-k sampling that scans the whole file, at the honest cost of decompressing the full ~100 GB stream. The chosen strategy is recorded in the result artifact (sample_strategy), and `head` is retained only for smoke tests. This removes a bias that inflated the project's own numbers.

findings.evidence: shlex.quote no bash -c de _ensure_sample (CWE-78). commit 75216ae
findings.message: `_ensure_sample` monta uma string de shell e a executa via `bash -c`, interpolando `path` NAO-quotado na redirecao `> {path}`. `path` deriva do arg CLI `--cache` (`args.cache`), controlado pelo operador — um valor com metacaracteres (espaco, `;`, `$(...)`) quebra o comando ou injeta (CWE-78 / OWASP A03). `_UA` e `HITS_TSV_GZ` sao constantes e `inner` e numerico (int-cast), entao o unico taint e `path`.
findings.remediation: Nao interpolar o caminho no shell: redirecionar via `stdout=open(path, 'wb')` e remover `> {path}` do comando, OU usar `shlex.quote(path)`. Fonte->sink: `--cache` (CLI) -> `bash -c`.

findings.evidence: extraida _bench_query; ruff PLR0915 passa. commit 75216ae
findings.message: run() is a large multi-responsibility orchestrator: MEASURED ruff PLR0915 = 68 statements (> 50), McCabe CC = 10 (at the default ceiling). One method prepares the dataset, opens the connection, runs the per-query loop, canonicalizes results and builds the report — several reasons to change.
findings.remediation: Extract cohesive stages out of run() (e.g. `_prepare_dataset(args)`, `_execute_queries(conn, queries, args)`, `_build_result(base, rows)`) so each has one reason to change; keep run() as the thin orchestrator (target < 50 statements / CC < 10).

findings.evidence: Line 161: `cur.execute(create_sql.replace("USING theodb_columnar", "").replace("hits", "hits_heap"))`. Line 218: `cur.execute(ab_sql.replace("hits", "hits_heap"))`. Both are unbounded `str.replace` substring substitutions.
findings.message: The heap-copy DDL and A/B query are derived by GLOBAL substring replacement of 'hits': line 161 `create_sql.replace("USING theodb_columnar", "").replace("hits", "hits_heap")` and line 218 `ab_sql.replace("hits", "hits_heap")`. `str.replace` rewrites EVERY occurrence of the substring 'hits', not just the table token, so any identifier/literal containing 'hits' would be silently mangled — breaking the byte-identical A/B correctness oracle. It works only because the current ClickBench schema/queries happen to contain no other 'hits' substring; it is a latent contract fragility, not a guaranteed-correct rewrite (naming/contract; KISS says target the table, not a substring).
findings.remediation: Replace on a word boundary: `re.sub(r"\bhits\b", "hits_heap", sql)`, or build the heap DDL/query from a parameterised table name rather than string-editing the columnar SQL.

findings.evidence: main() exit code != 0 se A/B diverge (fail-loud). commit 75216ae
findings.message: `sys.exit(main())` but `main()` (line 251) has no `return`, so it returns None and the process ALWAYS exits 0 — even when the byte-identical A/B oracle records `result_ab.diverged > 0`, whose verdict string is literally 'DIVERGENCE — pushdown bug' (run(), line 241). A detected columnar-vs-heap correctness divergence — the very oracle this harness exists to add over ClickBench — therefore does not fail the process, so a CI step chained on exit status proceeds as if the run passed. Violates fail-loud/fail-fast (rules/error-handling.md §1-§2: return explicit errors, do not exit 0 on failure).
findings.remediation: Have main() return a non-zero code on failure, e.g. `rc = 0 if data['status']=='OK' and data.get('result_ab',{}).get('diverged',1)==0 else 1; return rc` (or raise SystemExit with that code).

findings.evidence: line 54: `        import inspect` inside `test_systematic_e_o_default`, while `os`/`sys`/`unittest`/`mock` are imported at module top (lines 12-15).
findings.message: `import inspect` sits inside the test method body rather than at module top. PEP 8 places imports at the top of the file; a function-local import here buys nothing (no cost/cycle concern) and diverges from the file's own top-level import block.
findings.remediation: Move `import inspect` to the top-of-file import block.

findings.evidence: Line 1186: `*value = pg_sys::Datum::from(flat);` mutates `(*slot).tts_values[i]`. Lines 1196-1198: `for flat in owned { pg_sys::pfree(flat as *mut std::os::raw::c_void); }` frees those pointers; there is no code path restoring `(*slot).tts_values` to the pre-detoast datums.
findings.message: After the varlena materialisation loop replaces `*value = pg_sys::Datum::from(flat)` in the executor's slot (line 1186), `accumulate_row` frees each `flat` with `pg_sys::pfree` (lines 1196-1198) but never restores the original datums — so `(*slot).tts_values[i]` is left pointing at freed memory, a dangling pointer inside a caller-owned `TupleTableSlot`. It is safe TODAY only because the executor re-materialises the slot (slot_getallattrs) before any subsequent read; any future caller that reads `tts_values` after `columnar_tuple_insert`/`columnar_multi_insert` returns (without a re-deform) would hit use-after-free. Principle: do not leave dangling references in a structure you do not own (memory-safety contract).
findings.remediation: Snapshot the original datums before overwriting and restore them after `heap_freetuple`/`pfree`, or add a comment at the callback boundary asserting the slot is consumed and must not be read post-insert.

findings.evidence: columnar.rs:1206-1234: "the budget check happens BEFORE the row is pushed ... a single wide value (varlena allows up to 1 GB) would be copied in whole before any check, and the flush would only fire on the NEXT row. That would trade a loud INSERT error for a backend OOM." needs_flush_first guards on !p.rows.is_empty() && p.bytes.saturating_add(bytes.len()) > mwm; a lone over-budget row still flushes immediately (:1232). DoD: RSS < 2x maintenance_work_mem (plan :360).
findings.message: Backpressure / bounded write memory (maintenance_work_mem budget) — addressed: with rows now materialised at ingestion, the flush-budget check was correctly moved BEFORE the row is pushed (needs_flush_first), and the pending accounting (p.bytes) now reflects the materialised size rather than an 18-byte pointer. This keeps the pending buffer O(maintenance_work_mem) and prevents a single wide varlena (up to 1 GB) from piling on top of already-buffered rows and turning a loud INSERT error into a backend OOM (edge-case EC-1).
